data.name: Zachariah
data.gender_notes: Zachariah is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name 'Zachar' meaning 'remembered' and 'Yah' meaning 'God'. In the Old Testament, Zachariah was a priest who was miraculously given a son despite his old age, and the child was named John the Baptist. The name Zachariah carries the meaning “God remembered” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Zachariah usually hope their child will grow to embody god remembered and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of God's presence and faithfulness.
data.etymology: Zachariah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God remembered.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Zachariah total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_latin.name: Zachariah
in_latin.meaning: God has remembered, divine memory, or remembrance of God
in_latin.long_meaning: Zachariah is a Latinized form of the Hebrew name , derived from zāchar, meaning 'to remember,' and the suffix -iah, indicating a divine or heavenly origin. In the Bible, Zachariah is the name of a high priest and the father of John the Baptist, as mentioned in the Gospel of Luke. The name has been in use since ancient times and is still a popular choice among Christians today, symbolizing God's remembrance and love for humanity.

in_english.name: Zachariah
in_english.long_meaning: The name Zachariah is derived from the Hebrew language, and it means 'God remembers'. In the Bible, this name is found in various scriptures, including the Old Testament book of Isaiah (1:1) and the New Testament books of Luke and John. Zachariah was the father of John the Baptist, and he was visited by the angel Gabriel to announce the birth of this important religious figure.

data.cultural_impact: In Christianity, Zachariah is most notably known as the father of John the Baptist, who prepared the way for Jesus' ministry. He is considered a model of faith for his belief in God's ability to bring about miracles, even in the face of his advanced age and divine intervention with his ability to speak after the birth of his son.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Zachariah holds a deep spiritual significance, as it is a reminder of the importance of remembrance in our relationship with God. It can be seen as a call to remember and hold in our hearts the promises and faithfulness of God, even when it seems impossible or beyond our understanding. The name also reminds us of God's power and ability to bring about miracles, no matter our circumstances or age.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Zachariah, meaning "the Lord remembers," symbolizes the faithful trust in God's promises, even when they seem impossible or delayed. It is a reminder that God keeps His covenants and that He is always mindful of His people.

biblical_reference.note: Zachariah was a high priest who served during the time of the Second Temple in Jerusalem and was the father of John the Baptist.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Born a priest in the Hebrew Bible, son of Barachiah and grandson of Jehoiada. The name Zachariah carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
Name of a high priest in the New Testament who was visited by the angel Gabriel to announce the birth of his son, John the Baptist.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Zachariah remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.
